title: Rollback Broker: Cohesive Handshake Promoter for A/B + Shadow Orchestration
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces the Rollback Broker controller and operator-visible policy for multi-lane rollbacks (canary/A-B/shadow). Backward compatible: config defaults preserve existing behavior.
description: Why: We need a single decision plane that can reliably coordinate rollback actions across canary, A/B, and shadow lanes while preserving observability and auditability. Existing scripts and heuristics were duplicated across promotors, leading to inconsistent rollback timing and missing correlated telemetry. What: Adds a lightweight "Rollback Broker" service and a Promoter shim that performs a handshake with rollout lanes to decide deterministic rollback, backoff, or staged drain. The Broker exposes an opinionated policy adapter that can evaluate: - multi-metric gates (latency/err/quality) - cohort-level cooldowns and credits - synthetic smoke / canary dry-run scoring - audit ledger for replayable decisions How: - New controller: rollout/rollback_broker_controller.go implementing the broker state machine - Promoter shim: promoter/handshake_shim.go to unify canary, AB, and shadow promoters behind a single API - Policy DSL: policy/rollback_policy_v1.yaml and runtime adapter - Ledger: telemetry/rollback_ledger (append-only protobuf records) - E2E harness: tests/e2e/rollback_broker_smoke_test.go - Telemetry: metrics, traces, and events (console integration) Compatibility: The broker is opt-in via cluster rollout config; default remains original promoters. Rollback behavior can be toggled per-rollout and per-cohort. Checklist: - [x] Controller and promoter shim implemented - [x] Policy adapter + default policy shipped - [x] Ledger + protobuf schema added - [x] Unit tests for policy evaluation - [x] E2E smoke for canary + shadow handshake - [x] Console eventing + dashboard links - [x] Documentation and runbook draft - [x] Feature flag gating in operator config Notes: - Policy is intentionally conservative by default (prefer staged drain over immediate abort) - Ledger events are stored in telemetry bucket and can be replayed for incident analysis - This PR includes migration code to annotate in-flight rollouts so operator can pick correct decision path Related: ENG-2148 (unify promoter interfaces), SUP-4312 (customer incident: inconsistent canary rollback), ENG-2179 (telemetry ledger design)
